subject.title: unsafe plugin path error after onboarding

question: Should this installer fix the unsafe pnpm plugin manifest path directly, wait for upstream OpenClaw package provenance, or treat release pinning as the supported mitigation?
rationale: Changing the package manager, trusted install path, default release behavior, or release-pinning contract affects the installer’s security boundary and user-facing upgrade policy, so automation should not choose it without maintainer intent.

options.title: Verify current release first
options.body: Run or request a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 install on current main with current `openclaw@latest`, then choose installer-side or upstream ownership from the observed result.

options.title: Adopt release pinning
options.body: Review and merge https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-ansible/pull/50 if maintainers want the installer to support deliberate known-good release selection while keeping `latest` as the default.

options.title: Move fix upstream
options.body: If current OpenClaw packaging now makes fresh installs safe, close this only with upstream package/version provenance and leave the installer defaults unchanged.

recommendation.title: Verify current release first
recommendation.body: Run or request a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 install on current main with current `openclaw@latest`, then choose installer-side or upstream ownership from the observed result.

likelyOwner.reason: Alec Olson is the strongest history match for the current OpenClaw release package path and docs that define release-mode installs.
